name: time_manipulation
description: Exploitable reliance on block.timestamp for exact-equality checks, randomness, or short-window logic
question: The source file in `source` contains Solidity contract code that uses `block.timestamp` (or `now`) in a security-relevant way, and either (a) compares it with exact equality (`==`) to a deadline/target time, (b) uses it as a source of randomness or entropy, or (c) enforces a cooldown/lock window short enough (e.g. under ~15-30 seconds, or comparable to block time) that a validator's timestamp manipulation could bypass the intended restriction or unfairly shift financial outcomes such as auction price or vesting cliff.
criteria: `if (block.timestamp == ...)` or similar exact-equality comparison on a timestamp deadline
`block.timestamp` (or `now`) used to seed or compute a random value, e.g. `keccak256(abi.encodePacked(block.timestamp, ...))` for randomness
A short cooldown/rate-limit check comparing `block.timestamp - lastAction[msg.sender] < COOLDOWN` where COOLDOWN is a small constant (seconds to low minutes)
Cliff-style vesting or unlock that pays out a full amount immediately once `block.timestamp >= cliff` with no linear scaling, exploitable via timestamp shifting
Epoch-based reward/price calculation keyed directly off `block.timestamp / EPOCH_DURATION` without boundary buffers, enabling straddling manipulation
Dutch-auction or other decreasing-price logic computed directly from `block.timestamp` elapsed time without bounding validator drift impact
